[LFST.1.3] **The engine must emit completely, and the obligation is
unconditional.** The engine must emit, through the callback surface
([NCBK.2.1]), every event of every class: an inject-class event for every
input it consumed, a compare-class event for every observable it produced,
and every clock value it observed ([RFCS.17.1]). The engine must emit whether
or not a subscriber is registered, and must not let anything downstream of an
event decide whether that event is emitted.

An integrator may subscribe to all, some or none of that surface, and may
record or discard what it receives. Neither choice is a conformance question,
and neither is the engine's to constrain.

**An integrator that records the whole surface therefore holds a replayable
event trace by construction**, having done nothing further. Replayability is
not a recording discipline the integrator must follow; it is a guarantee the
engine owes. A trace is unreplayable only where a subscriber filtered
([LFST.9.2.1]).

**All or nothing, never selectively.** An engine with no stream surface at all
— a `constspace` target, or a `realtime` one configured without one — emits
nothing and produces no trace, which is a coherent state. What the engine must
not do is emit some kinds and withhold others: a trace missing one kind reads
as complete and is not, and nothing in it says otherwise.

The recording hook sits at step (1) of the consumption loop — on arrival,
before evaluation ([RARC.5.8.10]) — precisely so that what an event did
downstream cannot decide whether it was emitted. [RFCS.6.7] reasons to this
conclusion for one atom; it holds for all of them.
